s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive symmetric small joint pain with morning stiffness and fatigue
salient_findings: Symmetric pain in small joints of hands, wrists, knees, and ankles
Early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
Severe fatigue throughout the day
Recent mild COVID-19 infection
Elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
Synovitis and tenosynovitis on MRI
key_facts: 4 months of progressively worsening symptoms
Symmetric joint pain
Early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
Severe fatigue throughout the day
Recent mild COVID-19 infection confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR
No fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss, rash, or appetite changes since recovering from COVID-19
No recent genitourinary or gastrointestinal infections
No history of psoriasis or uveitis
Family history of rheumatoid arthritis
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 13 mm/hour
C-reactive protein of 4.3 mg/L
Antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640
Rheumatoid factor of 62.29 IU/mL
Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody of 237.39 units
Hepatitis B and C serologies were negative
Radiographs of hands, knees, ankles, and feet were unremarkable
Hand ultrasound showed no joint erosion
MRI of hands demonstrated synovitis and tenosynovitis

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: High levels of rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, symmetric small joint pain, morning stiffness, and family history of rheumatoid arthritis

shortlist.label: Seronegative Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar symptoms to rheumatoid arthritis but with negative serology for rheumatoid factor, although patient has high rheumatoid factor levels

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640 and overlapping symptoms with various connective tissue diseases

shortlist.label: COVID-19 associated arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent history of COVID-19 infection and development of arthritis symptoms

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: High antinuclear antibody titer and presence of fatigue, although other specific lupus criteria are not met

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of symmetric joint pain, early morning stiffness, and severe fatigue, combined with laboratory results showing elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, are consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis. The presence of synovitis and tenosynovitis on MRI also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Seronegative Rheumatoid Arthritis
rejected.why: The patient has positive serology results, including elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, which contradicts the definition of seronegative rheumatoid arthritis

rejected.label: Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: While the patient has some features of connective tissue disease, such as a high antinuclear antibody titer, the presence of specific autoantibodies and clinical features more strongly supports a diagnosis of Rheumatoid Arthritis

rejected.label: COVID-19 associated arthritis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms began after COVID-19 infection, but the presence of specific autoantibodies and clinical features more strongly supports a diagnosis of Rheumatoid Arthritis rather than a post-infectious arthritis

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient lacks other characteristic features of lupus, such as renal involvement, skin rash, or specific autoantibodies like double-stranded DNA antibodies
